Tapez la nouvelle taille en pixels, en pourcentage, ou sous forme de la résolution qu'elle donne à sa taille sur la page. Avec Conserver les proportions actif, la hauteur suit la largeur. Choisissez la méthode : Doux (photos), au départ ; Net, un peu plus précis ; Pixels durs (pixel art) : chaque pixel reste un carré d'une seule couleur ; Agrandir avec détails : doux, puis accentué quand l'image grandit. Cliquez sur OK. La boîte de dialogue affiche la taille d'origine, la nouvelle taille et la mémoire occupée par la nouvelle image. Quand plusieurs images bitmap sont sélectionnées, chacune est mise à l'échelle du même facteur. Redresser l'image Images bitmap > Redresser l'image corrige les photos inclinées, vues de biais ou déformées par l'objectif.  Utilisez la Grille (sa taille et sa couleur sont réglables) pour aligner l'image. Réglez les curseurs : Corriger la distorsion de l'objectif (de -100 à 100), Faire pivoter l'image (de -15 à 15 degrés), Perspective verticale et Perspective horizontale (de -100 à 100). Les boutons de rotation tournent d'abord l'image d'un quart de tour. Avec Recadrer l'image actif, le résultat est recadré au plus grand rectangle aux proportions d'origine ; Recadrer et rééchantillonner à la taille d'origine lui redonne le nombre de pixels d'origine. Sans recadrage, les coins sont transparents. Cliquez sur OK. Réinitialiser remet tous les réglages. Zoomez et déplacez l'aperçu avec les outils situés au-dessus. Le résultat remplace les pixels : les effets appliqués à l'image deviennent donc définitifs. Agrandir le cadre des images bitmap Certains effets, comme les flous, débordent des bords d'une image bitmap. Images bitmap > Gonfler l'image bitmap > Gonfler automatiquement l'image bitmap (actif au départ) agrandit les images bitmap de ce dont leurs effets ont besoin, avec une marge transparente. Gonfler manuellement l'image bitmap agrandit à la main les images bitmap sélectionnées : pour la largeur et la hauteur, tapez la nouvelle taille en pixels ou en pourcentage (de 100 à 1000 %), avec Conserver les proportions. L'image reste centrée.  Autres commandes bitmap Recadrer l'image bitmap recadre une image bitmap avec l'outil Recadrer ; faire glisser un coin d'une image bitmap avec l'outil Forme la recadre aussi. Modifier l'image bitmap ouvre l'image bitmap dans un autre programme. Supprimer l'arrière-plan avec l'IA rend transparent le fond d'une photo. Supprimer l'arrière-plan: Supprimer l'arrière-plan. Rompre le lien et Mettre à jour depuis le lien agissent sur les images bitmap liées à un fichier. Save Bitmap As enregistre une image bitmap dans un fichier PNG.

h: The dialog box Choosing the view Zooming and panning Picking colors on the preview
x: The Before and After preview Every dialog box that changes a picture shows the picture before and after the change in the same preview: Trace Bitmap, Remove Background, the color mode dialog boxes (Black and White, Duotone, Paletted), every bitmap effect and Image Adjustments. This page explains how to look at the picture there. The dialog box These dialog boxes are windows you size: drag an edge or a corner, or click the maximize button in the title bar. The preview fills the left of the window and grows with it; the dialog box's own settings sit in a column on the right, with OK and Cancel under them. The preview follows every change of the settings by itself. While you drag a slider it shows a quick, smaller version at once, and the full view when you let go. Nothing is worked out again while the settings stay the same, so the dialog box stays quick on large pictures. Choosing the view The Preview list above the picture chooses what the preview shows: Before and After (the default): the picture above and the result below. Before and After side by side: the picture on the left and the result on the right. Before: only the picture as it is. After: only the result. Wireframe overlay (Trace Bitmap only): the curves of the trace drawn over the picture, to see how closely they follow it. Before and After split (Image Adjustments only): one picture, the original on the left of a dashed line and the result on its right. Drag the line to move it. Image Adjustments starts on After. The labels Before and After sit in the corners of the panes. Transparent parts of the picture show a checkerboard. Zooming and panning The buttons beside the list: Zoom to fit (pressed at first) shows the whole picture in a pane. Zoom out and Zoom in zoom out and in by a quarter each click. The pan button (pressed at first) lets a drag on a pane move the picture. The wheel over a pane zooms about the pointer, so the spot under it stays in place. The two panes always share one zoom and one place: panning or zooming one moves the other the same way, so you compare the same spot. Image Adjustments also has Rotate left and Rotate right, which turn the view a quarter turn (the picture itself does not turn), and 100 %, which shows one pixel of the picture per point of the screen. A spinning mark after the pan button means the dialog box is still working out the result, such as a trace of a large picture; the window keeps answering meanwhile. Picking colors on the preview Some dialog boxes have an eyedropper that picks a color from the picture, such as the background color to remove. While it is on, a click on a pane takes the color under the pointer and the pan button is released. Click the pan button to stop picking. See also Tracing bitmaps, Removing the background, Bitmap color modes and Bitmap effects.

h: Vectorisation rapide La boîte de dialogue de vectorisation
x: Vectoriser des images bitmap La vectorisation transforme une image bitmap en formes vectorielles que vous pouvez modifier, recolorer et mettre à l'échelle sans perte de qualité : un logo numérisé, un croquis, une photo. Vectorisation rapide Sélectionnez une image bitmap et choisissez Images bitmap > Vectorisation rapide. Elle utilise le préréglage choisi dans la page Vectorisation de bitmaps des options globales (Clipart au départ). Repeat Last Trace vectorise à nouveau le bitmap sélectionné comme la dernière vectorisation, sans la boîte de dialogue, et Open Last Trace Settings ouvre la boîte de dialogue avec ses paramètres. Le menu contextuel d'un bitmap propose aussi ces commandes, avec Vectorisation par ligne centrale et Vectorisation par contour. La boîte de dialogue de vectorisation Images bitmap > Vectorisation par contour et Vectorisation par ligne centrale listent des préréglages ; choisissez-en un pour ouvrir la boîte de dialogue de vectorisation. Vectorisation par contour remplit les zones de couleur avec des formes : Dessin au trait, Logo, Logo détaillé, Clipart, Image basse qualité et Image haute qualité. Vectorisation par ligne médiane suit les lignes avec des courbes ouvertes : Illustration technique et Dessin linéaire.  La boîte de dialogue montre l'image bitmap avant et sa vectorisation après, mise à jour à mesure que vous changez les réglages : les boutons de préréglage en haut ; Détail (de 0 à 100) : plus de détail conserve des zones plus petites ; Lissage (de 0 à 100, 25 au départ) : des courbes plus douces, moins de nœuds ; Lissage des angles (de 0 à 100) : des angles plus arrondis ; Noir et blanc, ou le nombre de Couleurs (de 1 à 256) ; Supprimer le fond (actif au départ) : omet la couleur de fond ; Supprimer l'image d'origine (inactif au départ) ; Aperçu compte les courbes de la vectorisation complète. Cliquez sur OK pour vectoriser. Les formes sont placées sur l'image bitmap, les plus foncées en premier.

t: Masquer des couleurs dans les images bitmap
h: Pour masquer des couleurs
x: Masquer des couleurs dans les images bitmap Le panneau Masque bitmap masque ou conserve les pixels de couleurs choisies dans une image bitmap, par exemple pour rendre transparent un fond blanc. Ouvrez-le avec Images bitmap > Masque bitmap.  Pour masquer des couleurs Sélectionnez une image bitmap. Prélevez des couleurs dans les dix emplacements de couleur : cliquez sur la pipette, puis sur des couleurs de l'image ; chacune remplit l'emplacement sélectionné et le coche ; ou cliquez sur Sélectionner les couleurs de l'image pour remplir les emplacements avec les dix couleurs les plus utilisées par l'image. Sélectionnez un emplacement et réglez sa tolérance (de 0 à 100 %) : l'écart permis entre la couleur d'un pixel et celle de l'emplacement pour qu'ils correspondent encore. Choisissez Masquer la sélection (les pixels correspondants deviennent transparents) ou Afficher la sélection (seuls les pixels correspondants restent visibles, au départ). Cliquez sur Appliquer. Enregistrer le masque et Ouvrir un masque conservent les emplacements dans un fichier .msk ; Supprimer vide l'emplacement sélectionné. Chaque image bitmap change en une seule étape d'annulation.

t: Removing the background of a bitmap
h: To remove a background Options Tips
x: Removing the background of a bitmap Bitmaps > Remove Background makes the background of a photo or scan transparent and keeps the subject. It works on this computer and needs no AI service. The property bar of a selected bitmap has the same command.  To remove a background Select one or more bitmaps. Click Bitmaps > Remove Background. The preview shows the bitmap before and after, with a checkerboard where it becomes transparent. Set the options below until the subject stands out cleanly. Click OK. Every selected bitmap changes in one undo step. Options Background The colors to remove, one row each. At first there is one row, Automatic: TraceDraw learns the background's colors from the edges of the picture (up to four, so a gradient or a two-tone backdrop works). Each row has: its swatch; an eyedropper: click it, then click a color in a preview or on the drawing, and the row takes that color. On the first row, Automatic goes back to the learnt colors; its own tolerance, a whole number from 0 to 100. It shows the Tolerance below until you change it; Remove color (x), which takes the row out. The last row always stays. Add color (+) adds a row: click it, then click the color in the Before preview or on the drawing. A pixel counts as background when it is close enough to any color of the list, each color with its own tolerance. Shortcuts with the eyedropper on Shift+click in a preview adds the color under the pointer as a new row and keeps the eyedropper on, so you can pick several colors in a row. Alt+click takes out the row whose color is nearest to the one under the pointer. A color picked in a preview is taken from the picture before the change, so a part already removed can still be picked. Tolerance How far a color may be from the background's and still count as background (0 to 100, whole numbers). It is the tolerance of every row that has none of its own. Raise it when some backdrop stays; lower it when parts of the subject go. Edge softness Feathers the edge of the subject, in pixels. 0 keeps a hard edge. Contiguous (on at first) Only the background connected to the edges of the picture goes, so a white shirt on a white backdrop keeps its inside. A color picked in a preview also starts the removal from the point where you clicked, so a hole inside the subject can go with one pick. Turn it off to remove every pixel near a listed color, for example all the holes of a letter or a ring. Remove specks (on at first) Small loose spots left in the background go too. Clean edge colors (on at first) Takes the old background's color out of the half-transparent pixels of the edge, so no light or dark halo shows when the subject goes on another background. Reset puts every option back, with one Automatic row. OK remembers the options and the list of colors until you close TraceDraw, so the next Remove Background starts with them. Tips It works best on a backdrop that differs from the subject: a studio background, a sky, a product on a plain table. For busy scenes, the AI command Remove Background with AI (see AI) separates subject and scene by their meaning. The result replaces the pixels; effects on the bitmap are made permanent. To fine-tune afterwards, use Masking colors.

Impression TraceDraw imprime en créant un PDF des feuilles prêt pour l'impression, que la visionneuse de votre système envoie à l'imprimante. Ces pages expliquent la boîte de dialogue Imprimer et son aperçu, comment fusionner des données dans une composition pour en imprimer de nombreuses versions, comment vérifier un dessin avant l'impression et comment finir des banderoles avec une bordure et des œillets.

h: General Color Composite Layout Booklets Prepress PostScript and issues Print preview Other ways to print
x: Printing a drawing Choose File > Print (Ctrl+P). TraceDraw builds the sheets and sends them to the printer you choose, or opens a PDF of them in your system's viewer, where you choose the printer and print. In the browser version, the PDF is downloaded. Printing to a printer runs in the background: the window keeps working, the status bar says "Printing on ..." and then how the print went. The tabs are General, Color, Composite, Layout, Prepress, PostScript and Issues. Under them, Print preview opens the preview with these settings, and Apply keeps them for the next time.  General Destination: one of your system's printers, the system's PDF viewer (which then chooses the printer), a PDF file or a PostScript file. The gear button beside a printer opens its own settings, and the status, location and comment of the printer show under it. The dialog starts on the printer you printed to last. Orientation: match the layout, portrait or landscape. Sheet: the page's own size, the standard paper sizes, or a custom size you can save under a name. Print range: the whole document, the current page, a list of pages (such as 1-3, 5, 8-), or the selected objects; and all, odd or even pages of the document or of the list, for printing on both sides by hand. The selected objects print alone (nothing else of the page, its master layers or its background), on a page the size of the area they cover: with the sheet set to the page's size the paper is that area, on a fixed sheet they are centred at their size (smaller only when they do not fit, unless Keep page size is ticked), and the layouts repeat that area. Copies, collated as whole sets or not. Print as bitmap: each sheet becomes one picture at the resolution you give. Color Composite prints all colors on each sheet; Separations prints one gray page per ink (cyan, magenta, yellow, black, then each spot ink). In Print Preview you can untick inks under Print separations; only the ticked inks print. Convert spot colors to CMYK prints spot inks as their CMYK mix. Composite Print text in black. Always overprint black: full black fills and outlines print over the colors beneath. Layout As in document, Fit to page, or Scale to a percentage. Fit to page also shrinks objects larger than the page (or the selection, when you print only that) so they print whole on it. Bleed limit: how far beyond the page objects print (4 mm at first, or the drawing's own bleed). Paper margins (left, right, top, bottom, 0 at first) keep the paper's edges clear: the pages and their marks go in what is left. The imposition: several pages on one sheet, or a booklet, whose pages are paired for folding, with the sheet size and the gap between pages. A sketch shows the result. For the back of double-sided cards, tick Back side: the pages run right to left on the sheet, so each one prints behind its front, and the text is not mirrored. Keep page size keeps the pages at their size on a fixed sheet: they do not shrink for the marks, and the columns and rows stay as you set them (pages that do not fit run off the sheet, and a warning says so). Without it, the pages shrink to fit the columns and rows you ask for. In Print Preview, drag on the sheet to move the page information. Booklets Choose Booklet as the imposition to print two pages on each side of a sheet, ready to fold. Printing booklets explains it step by step. The page count is rounded up to a multiple of four with blank pages at the back, and the summary under the sketch says how many pages, blanks and sheets of paper it takes. To print only some of the pages, list them in Pages first. Binding: Saddle stitch nests every sheet inside the one before and staples them through the fold (8 pages: 8 1, 2 7 on the outer sheet). Perfect bound folds the sheets in signatures of Sheets per signature, stacks the signatures and glues them at the spine (one sheet per signature: 4 1, 2 3, then 8 5, 6 7). Creep (saddle stitch): how far the pages of the innermost sheet move toward the spine, so the fore edges line up after trimming; the sheets between move in proportion, the outer one not at all. Gap: the space between the two pages of a spread, centred on the fold. Prepress Invert and Mirror the whole sheet, for film. Print file information (the drawing's name or your own text, the page numbers, sheet number and date) and Print page numbers. Crop marks (and fold marks for booklets), Registration marks, Color bars and Densitometer scale. PostScript and issues With a PostScript file as the destination, the PostScript tab sets the language level (2 or 3). The Issues tab shows what the preflight check finds; see Preflight. Apply keeps the settings for the next time; see Global options for the defaults. Print preview File > Print Preview, or Print preview in the Print dialog box, shows the sheets exactly as they will print, with the imposition and the marks. The bar at the top has Print, the sheet shown with previous and next (PgUp, PgDn), the zoom with Fit, the printer with its settings button and status, the number of copies with Collate, and Close (Esc). On a narrow window the bar takes two rows. The options on the left stand two to a row: the pages (all, current, a list, the selection, odd or even), fit to page or the scale, then the prepress options (separations, bleed, marks, page information, mirror, invert, transform and artwork position), then the layout with its sketch. Every change rebuilds the sheets at once. Drag the panel's edge to make it wider. With Print separations on, a box for each ink stands under it. All ticked shows the sheet; one alone shows its plate in gray; some show the colors those inks print together. Drag the dashed blue lines on the sheet to set the paper margins, and drag the sheet to move the artwork on its page (Artwork position shows the move, with Reset). Transform draws handles to stretch the artwork. Other ways to print File > Send To saves a PDF to your desktop or documents folder, or attaches it to an email. Publi

h: Printing a booklet Choosing the binding The settings Blank pages and the counts
x: Printing booklets A booklet prints two pages on each side of a sheet of paper, placed so that the folded sheets read in order: a menu, a program, a small catalog or a zine. TraceDraw pairs the pages for you; you choose how the booklet is bound. Printing a booklet Put the pages of the drawing in reading order, the cover first. Choose File > Print (Ctrl+P) or Print Preview. On the Layout tab, choose Booklet as the Imposition. Under Binding, click one of the two pictures (see below). Set the binding's fields: Sheets per signature for a perfect-bound booklet, Creep for a saddle-stitched one, and the Gap for either. Check the sketch and the counts under it, then print on both sides of the paper. To make a booklet of only some pages, list them in the pages to print on the General tab first. Choosing the binding Saddle stitch (the default): every sheet is folded inside the one before and the booklet is stapled through the fold. For eight pages, the outer sheet holds pages 8 and 1 on one side and 2 and 7 on the other; the inner sheet holds 6 and 3, then 4 and 5. Best for thin booklets. Perfect bound: the sheets go in signatures, small groups of Sheets per signature (4 at first, 1 to 32) folded together. The signatures are stacked and glued at the spine. The last signature takes the sheets left over. With one sheet per signature the pages pair as 4 1, 2 3, then 8 5, 6 7. Best for thicker booklets. The settings Sheets per signature (perfect bound only): how many sheets are folded together in each signature. Creep (saddle stitch only, 0 to 20 mm, 0 at first): when nested sheets are folded, the inner ones stick out at the open edge and lose more when the booklet is trimmed. Creep moves the pages of the innermost sheet this far toward the spine; the sheets between move in proportion and the outer sheet does not move. The crop marks move with the pages. Gap (0 to 100 mm, 0 at first): the space between the two pages of a spread, centred on the fold. On a sheet sized to the pages, the sheet grows by the gap. Blank pages and the counts A booklet always has a multiple of four pages, since each sheet holds four. When the drawing has another number, blank pages are added at the back. Under the sketch, the summary gives the number of pages, the blank pages added and the sheets of paper printed on both sides, and for a perfect-bound booklet the number of signatures. With Crop marks on the Prepress tab, a booklet also gets a dashed fold mark at the spine. See Printing a drawing for the other marks. Tip: Print one copy first and fold it to check the order and the margins before you print them all.

h: Setting up a merge The Print Merge panel Kinds of field Editing the records
x: Print merge Print merge fills a design with data, to make many versions of it: name badges, numbered tickets, certificates, labels with QR codes. Each record of your data becomes a copy of the page, filled in. Setting up a merge Design the page. Where a value goes, type the field name in angle brackets in a text object, such as <Name>. Choose File > Print Merge > Create/Load Print Merge. Add the data: Import file reads a CSV file (separated by commas, semicolons or tabs, as Excel or any other program saves it) or an Excel workbook (.xlsx, its first sheet) whose first line names the fields. Fields named like a photo or a picture, or whose cells are picture files, start as pictures, fields named QR as QR codes; the types show at once to be changed; or Add column to add fields by hand, then add records with +. Click Finish. The Print Merge panel opens, where you put the fields on the page and make the merge.  The Print Merge panel The Print Merge panel (also under Window > Panels) works with the data source you created or loaded: Create and Edit open the records. Choose the kind of field, Text, Picture or QR code, and the column under Data source columns. For a picture, Pictures folder chooses the folder your photos are in, when the data names only their files (a name without an extension, such as 1024, finds 1024.jpg or 1024.png). Placeholder image chooses a picture that stands in for the merged ones while you design, and Align and scale sets where each picture goes in its frame: click one of the nine points to anchor it, then choose Actual size, Fit proportionally, Fill proportionally (the frame cuts what is outside) or Stretch to fill. Insert Field puts the field in the text you are editing, or places a new text, picture frame or QR square in the middle of the view. Move and size it like any object. To put each photo inside a shape of your own (a circle, an oval, any outline, also inside a grouped card design), choose Image and the photo column, select the shape and click Place Inside Frame. Every card's photo then goes inside that shape, placed by the alignment and scale. Tick On every page (off at first) before Insert Field to put a text, picture or QR code field in the same place on every page of the drawing. Create Merged Document then fills the drawing's own pages, one record each, instead of making a new drawing. Move or resize the field on its page and the copies on the other pages follow it when you merge; a copy you moved by hand on its own page stays where you put it. Select a field and click Update Field to change its column or its alignment and scale. Create Merged Document makes the merged pages in a new drawing: the page you are on is copied once per record and each copy is filled in. Your design stays as it is. Print Merged Document does the same and opens Print. Perform Merge instead adds the filled copies to the current drawing, right after the page, named after the page and the record number. Kinds of field Text: replaces <Field> in every text of the page. Number: a counter you do not type: a start, a step and a number of digits (start 7, step 3, digits 3 gives 007, 010, 013). Its Format is 1, 2, 3 (the default), A, B, C or a, b, c (1 is A, 26 is Z, then AA), or Custom, which puts a text of your own before and after the number, for tickets and serial numbers ("Ticket T-" before, 4 digits and start 98 give Ticket T-0098, Ticket T-0099 and so on). When you add a Number column, untick Continually increment value to give every record the same number, or give an ending value to make the records from the start to the end at once (15 to 25 in three digits makes eleven records, 015 to 025), with no data file at all. Picture: the cell holds the path of a picture. A text holding only <Field> becomes the picture, as large as fits its box. Put that text inside a frame with Place Inside Frame (a photo frame) and the picture fills the frame, cut by it. A rectangle, ellipse or curve named <Field> (in the Objects panel) takes the picture inside it the same way. Fields work in groups and frames too, so a card can be grouped. QR code: a text holding only <Field> becomes a QR code of the cell's text. An empty cell, or a picture that does not load, removes that object from the record's page. Editing the records Configure columns renames fields, changes their type and counter settings, and removes fields. View single record shows one record as a form; use the arrows or Go to record to move through them. The placeholder buttons insert a field into the text you are editing. Save data source writes the records as a CSV file. To work on several cells at once, drag from one cell to another, or over the record numbers or the field names to take whole records or fields. Then Add adds as many empty records after them, Delete removes their records and Clear (or the Delete key) empties the cells. Edit Print Merge reopens the records.

h: The checks Using the list
x: Preflight Preflight checks a drawing for what tends to go wrong in print, before you print it or send it to a print shop. Choose File > Preflight. The Print dialog box also runs the checks and shows how many issues it found.  The checks Empty text object text with nothing in it Text does not fit its frame paragraph text with hidden lines Font not installed text in a font that is not installed Very small text text smaller than 5 points as printed Small text in rich black small black text made of several inks RGB color in a CMYK drawing screen colors in a drawing meant for print Object off the page objects outside the page and its bleed Low-resolution bitmap bitmaps below 200 dpi as placed Very high-resolution bitmap bitmaps above 1200 dpi Very thin outline outlines thinner than 0.1 mm White set to overprint white that would vanish when printed Empty page pages with no objects Objects that will not print objects on hidden or non-printing layers Warnings are likely problems; notes are worth a look. Using the list The top of the box shows the outcome. Each kind of issue has a heading with its count; click it to open or close it. Click an issue to go to its page and select its object. Under the list, the box says what to do about the kind you picked. Check again runs the checks again after you fix things. Choose checks turns checks on and off and sets their limits: the bitmap resolutions, the smallest text sizes and the thinnest outline. Defaults puts them back.

h: Source Border Grommets
x: Border and grommets Tools > Border and Grommet finishes large prints such as banners and canvases: it grows the page by a border and places grommet marks, where the eyelets will be punched, along its edge.  The preview on the left shows the final page, the border band, the original area (dashed) and the grommets, with the final height and width. Source Choose Page, or Selection to make the box of the selected objects the page. Border Tick Add border and choose its type: Mirror the edges: the design is mirrored out into the border; Stretch the edges: the edge pixels are stretched out; Solid color: the border is filled with one color. Set the size (31.75 mm at first), the same on every side. The design stays where it is; mirrored and stretched edges are made from a picture of the design, placed behind it, so your objects stay editable. Grommets Tick Add grommets, then set: Use border area: center each grommet in the border band; Size: the diameter of the grommet (6.35 mm at first); Margin: from the outer edge to the grommet (31.75 mm at first). Under Placement and distribution, choose the edges (corners, top, bottom, left, right; all at first), then the number of grommets per edge (4 at first) or the spacing between them. Corner grommets are shared by the two edges. The grommets are drawn as thin circles on a layer of their own. Reset puts every field back; OK is available when a border or grommets are on.

Graphismes web Les graphismes pour les pages web, les applications et les écrans sont généralement des bitmaps (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) à la résolution de l'écran, ou des fichiers SVG qui restent nets à toutes les tailles. Ces pages expliquent comment les exporter un par un et comment exporter de nombreuses pages et objets à la fois. Les objets peuvent aussi porter des liens qui fonctionnent dans les fichiers SVG, HTML et PDF exportés ; voir Liens et signets.

h: Choosing a format Size and resolution Before exporting text
x: Exporting for the web File > Export For > Web opens the Export dialog box set up for screens: PNG at 96 dpi. It keeps its own settings, apart from Export. Office does the same for office documents (PNG at 150 dpi).  Choosing a format PNG: sharp edges and transparency; best for logos, icons and illustrations. JPEG: small files for photos; no transparency. Set the quality (1 to 100). WebP: small files with transparency; set the quality. GIF: few colors, with transparency. SVG: vector graphics that stay sharp at any size and keep links and object names. HTML: a web page with the drawing. Size and resolution For bitmap formats, set the resolution, or type the width or height in pixels: the other side follows the proportions of the page. For a 32 by 32 pixel icon, type 32. With Transparent background on, the empty parts of the page stay transparent in PNG, WebP and GIF files. Selected only exports only the selected objects, cropped to them; All pages exports every page. The preview shows what will be written, and the dialog box estimates the file size. Before exporting text Text > Make Text Web-compatible simplifies text for the web. To export many pages or objects at once, see The Export panel.

h: Adding assets Exporting
x: The Export panel The Export panel keeps a list of assets (pages and objects) and exports them all at once, each in its own format, to one folder: the icons of an app in several sizes, every page of a set of social media posts. Open it from Window > Panels.  Adding assets Add pages adds every page of the drawing, named after the page. Add selection adds the selected objects as one asset, cropped to them, named after the object. New assets take the format and resolution set under New assets (PNG at 150 dpi at first). Each asset has a tick (only ticked assets are exported), its name (the file name), its format, its resolution for bitmap formats (72 to 2400 dpi) and a cross to remove it. The link under the name goes to the page or selects the objects. Exporting Click Browse to choose the folder (the first export asks for one). Click Export. The button shows how many assets will be written. Characters that files cannot have in their name become _, and two assets with the same name get " (2)", " (3)" and so on. The status bar says how many files were written. In the browser, every file is downloaded.

Formats de fichiers TraceDraw enregistre son propre format, .tdraw, qui conserve tout, et enregistre aussi des fichiers .cdr. Il ouvre et importe de nombreux autres formats, et exporte des formats vectoriels, bitmap et d'impression. Ces pages listent les formats et expliquent l'importation, l'exportation et la publication de fichiers PDF.

h: Saving Opening and importing Exporting
x: Supported file formats Saving TraceDraw (.tdraw) the native format; keeps everything, including effects, styles, comments and fonts CDR (.cdr) versions 7 to 27 from Save As; keeps pages and their sizes, layers, shapes, curves, groups and their names, text, bitmaps, fills, outlines and transparency, and the fonts with Embed fonts. From version 14, blends, contours, distortions, envelopes, perspectives, extrusions, bevels, block shadows and symmetries open again in TraceDraw as live effects; other programs see the objects the effects drew. Drop shadows are written as a picture of the shadow under the object TraceDraw template (.tdt) from Save as Template A package (a folder) from Package: the drawing, its linked pictures, its fonts and a report; see Packaging a drawing Opening and importing TraceDraw (.tdraw, .tdt) everything CDR (.cdr), from the oldest versions to the newest pages, layers, shapes, curves, groups, text, bitmaps (CMYK pictures in the CMYK mode), fills including mesh fills, outlines, transparency, blends, embedded objects drawn as pictures (such as barcodes), embedded fonts, the color profile CMX pages, layers, shapes, fills, outlines, images, clips, text SVG, SVGZ shapes, groups, clips, gradients, images, text PDF, AI paths, images, text, clips, shadings, patterns; password-protected files ask for the password EPS, PS, PRN, older AI files paths, images, text, clips, shadings; one page per printed page DXF lines, polylines, arcs, ellipses, splines, hatches, text, blocks EMF, WMF paths, pens, brushes, text, bitmaps, clips PLT (HPGL) plotter pen strokes PSD, PSB the layers as bitmaps, with opacity, visibility and masks PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, WebP, TIFF bitmaps TXT, RTF, DOCX paragraph text with its formatting Exporting SVG, HTML vector, for the web PDF, AI vector, for print and sharing; PDF/X-1a, X-3 and X-4 EPS, PostScript (.ps), PRN vector, for print DXF, PLT vector, for CAD, plotters and cutters EMF, WMF vector, for office programs PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF bitmap PSD bitmap, one layer per layer of the drawing Scripts can add more formats to importing and exporting; see Scripts.

h: Where imported objects go Notes on some formats
x: Importing files File > Import (Ctrl+I) adds the content of a file to the drawing that is open, on the active layer, as one undo step. Open instead opens a file as a drawing of its own. Both read the formats listed in Supported file formats. Where imported objects go At first, imported objects go where the file has them. To center them in the view instead, change the setting on the File Formats page of the global options; see Global options. Notes on some formats PDF and AI: the Import PDF dialog box asks how to read the text: as editable text, which keeps its fonts when they are installed, or as curves, drawn from the fonts the file embeds so the text looks exactly as it does in the file. Options > File Formats keeps the choice. A protected file asks for its password in the Protected PDF dialog box. EPS and PostScript: each printed page becomes a page. PSD: each layer becomes a bitmap with its opacity, visibility and mask. DXF: drawing units are taken from the file. Text files (TXT, RTF, DOCX): become paragraph text, with bold, italic, sizes and fonts where the file has them. Bitmaps: placed at their resolution; see Bitmaps. When some objects of a file cannot be read, or fonts are missing, a message says so; see Notes after opening. You can also drag files onto the window, or paste from other programs; see Paste Special.

h: To export Format options Size of bitmaps Presets Starting choices
x: Exporting File > Export (Ctrl+E) writes the drawing, a page or the selection in another format. The Export dialog box shows a preview on the left and the settings on the right.  To export Choose File > Export. Choose a Preset to start from saved choices, or choose the format. The common formats (JPG, PDF, AI, PNG) are first. Choosing a format brings back the settings you used for it last. Set the format's options (below). Tick Selected only to export only the selection, or All pages to export every page. Click OK and choose where to save. In the browser, the file is downloaded. The dialog box estimates the size of the file and, for bitmap formats, says what comes out, such as "1240 x 1754 pixels, 150 dpi, sRGB". With Do not show filter dialog ticked, the next export goes straight to the file with the same choices. Format options PNG, WebP, GIF resolution (or the size in pixels), transparent background; WebP also quality JPEG resolution, quality (1 to 100) BMP, TIFF, PSD resolution PDF standard (PDF 1.4, PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3 or PDF/X-4), bleed, output condition for PDF/X PDF, AI title and tags SVG, EPS, AI, DXF, HTML, EMF, WMF, PLT, PS, PRN none Size of bitmaps For bitmap formats, Size has a width, a height and their unit (px, mm, cm or in); the other side follows the page's proportions. In pixels, typing a width or height sets the resolution that gives it, so you can type the size of an icon (32 x 32 pixels) directly. In a length, the size is the printed size: typing a width or height scales the artwork at the resolution you set, from 1 % to 10000 %. A button with the scale (such as "200 %") shows when it is not 100 % and puts it back. PNG, JPEG and BMP files record their resolution, so they open at the size you chose. PostScript and PRN files hold every exported page. Presets The Preset list holds every preset you saved, each with its format in brackets, such as "Web PNG (PNG)". Choosing a preset of another format switches the dialog to that format; changing the format leaves no preset chosen. + saves the current choices under a name (the same name replaces that preset), the pencil renames the chosen preset and - deletes it. Starting choices The starting choices are set on the File Formats page of the global options, where Remember the settings of the last export (on at first) makes the dialog start with the format, resolution and quality of the last export, in the next session too. Export For has presets for the web and for office documents; see Exporting for the web. For PDF files with bookmarks and security, use Publishing to PDF.

h: General Color Document Objects Bitmaps Prepress Text and fonts Security Issues Opening protected PDF files
x: Publishing to PDF File > Publish to PDF (also on the standard toolbar) writes a PDF file with full control of what goes in: which pages, which PDF standard, how pictures are compressed, document information, bookmarks, printers' marks and password protection. The tabs are General, Color, Document, Objects, Prepress, Security and the issues tab.  General File name, with Browse to choose another place. Export range: the current document (every page), every open document, the current page, a list of pages (such as 1-3, 5), or the selection. Page size for a selection: Defined by document (the page, with only the selected objects) or Defined by selected objects (a page the size of the selected objects, the default). PDF preset: Document Distribution, Web, Prepress (PDF/X-4), PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3, or your own; + saves the current settings as a preset under a name you type (the same name replaces it) and - deletes the chosen one. A preset sets the compatibility, the output condition, the flattening resolution, the bookmarks, the bleed, the printers' marks and the bitmap choices. Compatibility: PDF 1.4, PDF/X-1a:2003, PDF/X-3:2003 or PDF/X-4. PDF/X files are made for print shops. Color For PDF/X, the output condition (FOGRA39 at first); the CMYK profile of the drawing goes into the file. A plain PDF keeps the colors as they are. Document Title, Author, Subject and Keywords, filled in from the drawing's properties; a bookmark for each page (on at first) and show the bookmarks when the file opens. Objects Flatten transparency at a resolution (300 dpi), for PDF/X-1a and X-3, which do not allow transparency. The other standards keep transparency live, so the field is greyed for them. Bitmaps The Bitmaps group sets how pictures go into the file. The choices are kept for the next time and in the presets. Downsample colour images to (off, 300 dpi): a colour picture with more pixels than this resolution, as it is placed on the page, is made smaller to that resolution. Downsample gray images to (off, 300 dpi): the same for pictures that are only grays. Gray pictures always go in with one channel, which keeps them small. Downsample black-and-white images to (off, 1200 dpi): the same for pictures of only black and white pixels. Compression: ZIP (lossless) (the default) keeps every pixel; JPEG makes smaller files with some loss, at the Quality you set (1 to 100, 85 at first). Black-and-white pictures, transparency masks and PDF/X-1a files always use ZIP. Compress text and line art (on) compresses the pages' text and drawing. A picture that lies wholly outside the page and its bleed cannot show, so it is left out of the file. The Web preset downsamples colour and gray pictures to 150 dpi and black-and-white ones to 300 dpi, with JPEG at quality 75. Prepress Bleed (0 to 50 mm, the drawing's bleed at first) around every page: the trim box is the page, the media box the page and the bleed. Printers' marks: Crop marks, Registration marks, Color bars and File information around every page. See Printers' marks in PDF files. Text and fonts Text goes into the PDF as real text: in a PDF viewer you can search it, select it and copy it, and it keeps its fill, outline, colors and angle. The fonts go into the file as well, so the text looks the same on any computer. In the Text and fonts group of the Objects tab: Export all text as curves (off at first) writes every text as curves instead: the file has no fonts and its text cannot be searched. The curves follow the letters' own outlines exactly, so they stay smooth at any zoom. Embed fonts in document (on at first) puts the fonts in the file. Turned off, the fonts are only named and the viewer uses its own copy. Embed base 14 fonts also puts Helvetica, Times and Courier in the file; otherwise the viewer's standard fonts draw them. Subset fonts puts in only the letters the file uses, which keeps it small, when a font uses less than the share you set (80 %). PDF/X files always carry their fonts. Some fonts do not allow being put in other files: their text is written as curves, the status bar names them after publishing, and the preflight lists such text beforehand. Security Require a password to open the file, and the password. Restrict printing, copying and changes with a password, and the password, then the permissions: printing (not allowed, low resolution only, allowed), copying, changing the content, adding comments, filling in forms, managing pages and text access for screen readers. Show passwords. PDF/X files cannot be protected. The passwords are never kept. Issues The last tab lists what the preflight check finds; see Preflight. Click OK to write the file. If something is missing, such as a password or a page in the list, the dialog box says so in red. Opening protected PDF files When you open or import a PDF that needs a password, the Protected PDF dialog box asks for it. Type the Password and click OK. A wrong password is refused and you can try again; Cancel leaves the file closed.

h: Adding the marks What the file looks like
x: Printers' marks in PDF files A print shop trims, registers and checks printed sheets with marks drawn outside the page: lines that show where to cut, targets that line up the plates, patches of ink and a line naming the file. The Prepress tab of File > Publish to PDF adds these marks around every page of the PDF, so the file can go to the press as it is. Adding the marks Choose File > Publish to PDF. On the Prepress tab, set the Bleed: how far the drawing runs past the edge of the page (the drawing's bleed at first, 0 to 50 mm). Objects that reach past the page print up to this line, so no white edge shows after trimming. Under Printers' marks, tick the marks you want (all are off at first): Crop marks: short lines (5 mm) in line with the edges of the page, starting 1.5 mm outside the bleed, that show where to cut. Registration marks: a target (a small circle with a cross) in the middle of each side, to line up the plates of each ink. Color bars: patches of the four process inks, the mixes of two of them and their 50 % tints, beside the top target, to check the inks on the press. File information: the drawing's name, the page's name, the page number and page count, and the date and time, under the page. Click OK. The Prepress (PDF/X-4) preset ticks Crop marks. The marks you tick are kept for the next time and in the presets you save with +. What the file looks like When any mark is ticked, each page of the PDF grows by a 12 mm margin outside the bleed, on every side, to hold the marks: The trim box, the size of the finished piece, is the page. The bleed box is the page and its bleed. The drawing is clipped to it, so nothing of it runs into the marks. The media box, the whole sheet of the PDF, takes in the bleed and the margin with the marks. A page background covers the bleed too. Links and bookmarks keep pointing at the page. The marks are drawn in the registration colour, so on a press they print on every plate, and they print the same in separations from a PDF viewer. Without any mark ticked the page is the page and its bleed, as before. Tip: The marks are the same ones the File > Print dialog box draws on its sheets (see Printing a drawing). Use the PDF when the print shop asks for a file; use Print when you print the sheets yourself.

h: Making a package Saving as a package What goes into the folder Opening a package
x: Packaging a drawing A drawing that links to picture files and uses fonts other computers may not have does not travel well as a single file. A package puts the drawing and everything it needs into one folder: the drawing, the pictures it links to, the font files its text uses, a report and, if you want, a PDF. Hand the folder to a print shop or a colleague, or keep it with the finished job. Note: Packages need the desktop version. In the browser version the menu command is greyed out and Save As does not offer the choice. Making a package Choose File > Package. In the Package Drawing dialog box, check the Folder. It is a new folder named after the drawing, in the folder of the drawing's file (else the folder you used last, else your home folder). Browse picks another place for it and keeps the folder's name. Check the File name of the drawing in the package (the drawing's name, as a .tdraw file). Tick Include a PDF to add a PDF of the drawing (off at first). Click OK. TraceDraw makes the folder when it does not exist and replaces files of the same names in it. The drawing you have open does not change: its links still point to the original pictures. The status bar says how many pictures and fonts went in, and how many items could not (the report names them). Saving as a package You can also package a drawing while you save it: Choose File > Save As. Choose TraceDraw (*.tdraw) as the Save as type. Tick Package and, if you want a PDF too, Include a PDF. Type the name and click Save. The drawing is saved as <name>/<name>.tdraw in the folder you chose, with its pictures copied beside it. Unlike Package, Save As changes the open drawing: its links now point to the copies in the package, so from then on you work on the package's drawing. What goes into the folder The drawing <name>.tdraw The drawing, with the fonts it already carries. Linked pictures Pictures folder Every picture the drawing links to, in groups, clip frames and symbols too, each file once. Two files of the same name are kept apart as logo.png and logo-2.png. Fonts Fonts folder One font file for each face the text uses, but only fonts whose licence allows them to go with a document. A PDF (optional) <name>.pdf Written with the choices you made last in Publish to PDF, with the drawing's bleed. A report <name> report.txt What went in, and what could not: pictures not found, fonts left out because of their licence, and fonts that are not installed with the font that draws their text. The links of the drawing in the package point to the copies as paths relative to the drawing (Pictures/logo.png), so you can move, copy or send the whole folder and the links keep working. A picture whose file is gone keeps its old link and is named in the report; its pixels are in the drawing anyway, so it still shows. Opening a package Open the .tdraw file of the package as any drawing. When the drawing's folder has a Fonts folder beside it, TraceDraw uses the fonts in it for this session, so the text shows in its own fonts even where they are not installed. Nothing is installed on the computer. Tip: Links relative to a drawing are read from the drawing's folder everywhere, also when a linked picture is updated from its file, so a package can live anywhere. To check the drawing before packaging it (missing fonts, pictures at low resolution, colours), run the preflight first.

Personnaliser et automatiser TraceDraw peut être réglé selon votre façon de travailler : options du programme et de chaque outil, apparence de l'interface, raccourcis clavier, barres et espaces de travail. Vous pouvez aussi automatiser le travail avec des scripts, connecter un service d'IA pour dessiner d'après une description et suivre le temps passé sur un dessin. Les options se trouvent dans Outils > Options : chaque élément ouvre sa propre boîte de dialogue. Les changements apparaissent tout de suite ; OK les garde et Annuler remet tout comme avant. Le bouton ? ouvre la page de cette Aide consacrée à la page d'options affichée.

Le réglage s'applique au prochain démarrage. Si la fenêtre ne peut pas s'ouvrir ainsi, TraceDraw redémarre avec le rendu logiciel, puis avec OpenGL, et garde celui qui a fonctionné. Visibility of inactive objects (20 % au départ) et Double-click to activate focus mode ; voir Mode focus. Nœuds et poignées  Taille du nœud : petite, moyenne ou grande. x: Options de personnalisation Traduction automatique : cette page peut être en retard sur la version anglaise. Outils > Options > Personnalisation règle l'apparence de l'interface, vos propres raccourcis clavier, les barres affichées et le comportement de la palette de couleurs. Apparence  Centrer les boîtes de dialogue : les boîtes de dialogue s'ouvrent au milieu de la fenêtre ; désactivé, elles s'ouvrent là où vous les avez laissées. Shadows under menus and dialogs (moins d'ombres aide les cartes graphiques lentes). Coloured tool icons : chaque groupe d'outils reçoit sa propre couleur. Taille : la taille des menus, des barres, des icônes et des panneaux, par rapport à la mise à l'échelle que votre système donne à l'écran (100 % au départ). Rétablir la valeur par défaut revient à 100 %. La taille de l'interface ne change jamais la taille de votre dessin. Grow with the desktop text size (now {n} %) la fait grandir avec la taille du texte du bureau. Couleur : le Thème (Clair, Moyen clair, Moyen sombre, Sombre ou Contraste élevé), Use high contrast while the desktop has a high contrast theme on, et la Couleur du bureau autour de la page. Le bouton à l'extrémité droite de la barre d'état bascule entre clair et sombre. Commandes  La page liste toutes les commandes des menus, avec leur raccourci, ainsi que les touches des outils. Tapez dans Rechercher pour filtrer la liste. Pour donner votre propre raccourci à une commande : Cliquez sur le bouton de raccourci de la commande. Appuyez sur les touches, par exemple Ctrl+Alt+K. Esc arrête l'attente. Vos raccourcis passent avant les raccourcis intégrés : quand vous prenez une touche utilisée par une autre commande, la page indique quelle commande l'a perdue. Les menus affichent votre raccourci. Le x à côté d'un raccourci le supprime, et la réinitialisation aux valeurs par défaut les supprime tous. Les touches des outils sont une lettre, ou Shift et une lettre. Voir Raccourcis clavier. Une commande peut avoir plusieurs raccourcis : une nouvelle touche s'ajoute à celles qu'elle a (une touche intégrée continue de marcher à côté), et chaque touche a son propre bouton de suppression. Les boutons des barres qui lancent une commande de menu (Nouveau, Ouvrir, Enregistrer, Annuler, Zoom avant et d'autres) prennent aussi des raccourcis, les mêmes touches que leur commande de menu, tout comme les lignes que les menus n'affichent que par moments. Une liste Boutons des barres d'outils contient tous les boutons des barres Standard et Zoom : faites glisser de là, vers sa barre, un bouton retiré. Barres de commandes  Afficher ces barres Barre de menus, Standard, Barre de propriétés, Boîte à outils, Barre d'état, Palette de couleurs, ainsi que les barres d'outils Texte, Zoom et Transformer. Réinitialiser remet les barres en place. Sous Autres : Verrouiller les barres et Afficher le menu contextuel Contour dans la boîte à outils. While these pages are open (or with Alt held), drag a button of the Standard or Zoom toolbar to move it, or off the bar to remove it. Drag a command from the Commands page onto one of these bars to add it. Reset on the Command Bars page brings the first buttons back. Palette de couleurs  Mettre à jour automatiquement la palette du document et Afficher la palette du document (actifs tous les deux). Échantillons de couleur : Afficher la case « Aucune couleur » (actif), et ce que fait le Bouton droit de la souris : Définir la couleur du contour (au départ) ou ouvrir le Menu contextuel. Voir Palettes de couleurs.

x: Tool options Tools > Options > Tools sets how tools behave and what new objects they draw. Most of these values are also on the property bar of each tool. Pick  Cross hair cursor: the pointer is a cross hair. Treat all objects as filled (on): clicking inside an unfilled object selects it. Marquee selects touched objects (off): a marquee also selects the objects it only touches; Alt then selects only those wholly inside. Zoom and Pan  Zoom tool, right mouse button: Zoom out (at first) or the Context menu. Default action for mouse wheel: Zoom or Scroll. Curves  Freehand smoothing: 0 to 100 (50 at first). Join and close within: how close to an end node a line must start to continue the curve (5 screen pixels at first). See Continuing a curve. Preview mode and Add and delete nodes automatically (both on) for the Pen tool; see Pen. Graphics tablet: Pen pressure sets the width of Freehand and Brush Strokes drags (on); see Drawing with a graphics tablet. Rectangle  Rectangle corners: Round Corner, Scalloped Corner or Chamfered Corner, the four corner sizes and Edit Corners Together. Scale corners: Relative Corner Scaling. Ellipse  Ellipse, Pie or Arc, with the Starting angle and Ending angle. Polygon  Number of points and Sharpness. Spiral  Revolutions, and Symmetrical spiral or Logarithmic spiral. Graph Paper  Rows and Columns of the grid. Table  Rows and Columns of new tables. Eraser  Eraser thickness (6.35 mm at first), and Round nib or Square nib.

x: Options globales Traduction automatique : cette page peut être en retard sur la version anglaise. Voir Imprimer un dessin. Mémoriser les réglages de la dernière exportation conserve les choix de la dernière exportation. Importer : Les objets importés vont Là où le fichier les place (au départ) ou Centrés dans la vue. Enregistrement des fichiers .cdr : la Version dans laquelle les nouveaux dessins sont enregistrés en .cdr. Vectorisation  La vectorisation rapide utilise l'un des préréglages (Clipart au départ). Avertissements  Afficher un message Lorsque des objets d'un fichier ouvert n'ont pas pu être lus, Lorsqu'un dessin ouvert utilise des polices non installées et Avant de retirer un élément de l'étagère (tous actifs). Chaque message a aussi une case qui le désactive ; cochez l'option ici pour le revoir. Ask which installed font draws each missing one (the Missing Fonts dialog) (activée) affiche la boîte de dialogue Polices manquantes quand un dessin s'ouvre avec des polices non installées ; voir Polices manquantes. Elle est distincte du simple message ci-dessus. Emplacements des fichiers  Indique où sont conservées les préférences et les sauvegardes automatiques. Les préférences se trouvent dans un dossier tracedraw-settings à côté du programme quand il existe (une copie portable), sinon à l'emplacement prévu par votre système pour les paramètres des programmes ; la version pour navigateur les conserve dans le navigateur.

h: Built-in workspaces What is kept Exporting and importing your setup
x: Workspaces A workspace is how the window is set up: which bars show and where, the toolbox, keyboard shortcuts, the color palette options and the look of the interface. Choose one in Window > Workspace, or on the Workspace page of Tools > Options > Workspaces.  Built-in workspaces Default: the usual setup. Lite: fewer bars, for a first start. Classic, Illustration and Page Layout: bars and panels for those kinds of work. Touch: for touch screens. The interface is drawn larger, rulers, panels and the status bar are hidden, and two fingers pan and pinch to zoom with any tool. Drawings keep their real size. What is kept Everything you change is kept when TraceDraw closes and comes back the next time: the options, where each bar sits and which bars show, the tool each toolbox group shows, the panels that are open, units, snapping, the settings new objects take and what the window shows. Exporting and importing your setup To carry your setup to another computer, or keep it safe: On the Workspace page, under Export and import, tick the parts to include: keyboard shortcuts; toolbars, toolbox and status bar; color palette options; appearance. Click Export and save the .tdws file. On the other computer, click Import and choose the file. Only the parts you ticked are applied. Window > Workspace > Export Workspace and Import Workspace do the same with every part.

h: Pour réinitialiser tous les paramètres
x: Réinitialiser les paramètres Si votre configuration s'emmêle, vous pouvez remettre toutes les préférences telles que TraceDraw les fournit. Vos dessins ne sont jamais touchés. Pour réinitialiser tous les paramètres Choisissez Rétablir tous les réglages dans la page Général de Outils > Options > Global. Ou appuyez sur F8 pendant que l'écran de démarrage s'affiche au lancement de TraceDraw. TraceDraw demande d'abord confirmation. Réinitialiser remet toutes les préférences, mais conserve la liste des dessins récents, le dernier dossier et la taille de la fenêtre. Annuler ne change rien.  Pour ne réinitialiser que certains éléments : la boîte à outils et les barres ont leurs propres commandes de réinitialisation (voir L'espace de travail), et choisir un espace de travail intégré règle ses propres barres (voir Espaces de travail).

h: Configurer le service d'IA Général Dessiner avec des mots Le panneau Génération IA Autres commandes d'IA
x: Dessiner et générer avec l'IA TraceDraw peut dessiner à partir d'une description en mots et créer des images avec un service d'IA que vous choisissez et configurez avec votre propre clé. TraceDraw n'a ni IA propre ni compte : rien n'est envoyé tant que vous ne lancez pas une commande d'IA, et seul ce dont la commande a besoin part alors vers le service configuré. Chaque requête est facturée par votre service ; les serveurs de modèles locaux sur votre ordinateur ne coûtent rien. Configurer le service d'IA Outils > Options > AI comporte deux pages.  Dans la page Service, configurez un service d'IA pour toutes les fonctions d'IA : Choisissez un Préréglage : Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, ou un serveur de modèles sur votre ordinateur (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp server, vLLM). Un préréglage remplit la sorte de service et l'adresse ; Personnalisé accepte toute adresse qui parle le même langage que les chat completions d'OpenAI. Tapez la Clé d'API de votre compte auprès de ce service (les serveurs locaux n'en ont pas besoin). Cochez Retenir la clé sur cet ordinateur pour la conserver ; elle est alors stockée en clair dans vos préférences. Choisissez le Modèle, et le Modèle d'image pour les services qui savent créer des images (OpenAI, Google Gemini, ou une adresse personnalisée avec un modèle d'image). Cliquez sur Test Connection. Il demande au service la liste de ses modèles et indique combien il en a, ou affiche son erreur. Afficher la barre d'invite place la barre d'invite d'IA au-dessus de la palette de couleurs. Général  Turn on AI features (actif) : désactivé, toutes les commandes d'IA sont grisées. Services : si Drawings et Pictures sont Ready ou Not set up. Features : ce que fait chaque commande d'IA. What is sent : seulement ce dont une commande a besoin, vers le service que vous avez configuré, au moment où vous la lancez. Dessiner avec des mots Tapez une demande comme "un vélo rouge aux roues bleues" ou "agrandis le cercle et mets le titre en dessous", dans la barre d'invite ou dans le mode Dessiner avec des mots du panneau AI Generate (Objet > AI Generate > Draw with Words), et appuyez sur Dessiner ou sur Entrée. Le service écrit un script pour le dessin, que TraceDraw exécute en une seule étape d'annulation. La conversation est conservée : vous pouvez donc demander des modifications ; Nouvelle conversation recommence. Ouvrir dans Scripts affiche le script. Le panneau Génération IA Le panneau AI Generate (Outils > AI Generate, ou le bouton de génération IA de la barre d'outils standard) crée des images avec le modèle d'image de votre service.  Choisissez un mode avec les boutons du haut : Créer une image : une image à partir d'une description. Inspire-moi propose une idée. Choisissez les proportions. Remixer une image : modifie une image selon votre description (l'image bitmap sélectionnée au départ). Les demandes prêtes à l'emploi comprennent maquette, restauration de photo, mise en couleur d'un croquis, remplacement du fond, changement de saison et recoloration. Créer des vecteurs : une illustration transformée en formes modifiables, soit une image vectorisée en courbes, soit un dessin SVG écrit par le modèle de texte. Dessiner avec des mots (voir ci-dessus). Chaque mode a un Modèle, une image de référence facultative (Utiliser la sélection ou Importer un fichier), l'Invite, et des vignettes Style et Palette de couleurs. En bas, réglez le nombre d'Images (de 1 à 4) et Insérer dans le dessin, puis cliquez sur Générer. Les résultats restent dans le panneau ; cliquez sur l'un d'eux pour l'insérer. Autres commandes d'IA Images bitmap > Supprimer l'arrière-plan avec l'IA garde le sujet d'une image et rend le reste transparent. AI Art Styles repeint la sélection dans l'un de huit styles. Tant que l'IA est désactivée ou non configurée, les commandes sont grisées et leur info-bulle explique pourquoi ; le bouton Set Up AI ouvre la bonne page d'options.

x: Scripts and automation Scripts automate repetitive work: draw shapes from data, change many objects at once, or add a file format. They are written in JavaScript in the Scripts panel (Tools > Scripts > Scripts Panel).  Writing and running scripts A script works with the objects of TraceDraw: Application, ActiveDocument, ActivePage, ActiveLayer and the shapes, fills, outlines, colors, curves and effects. For example: Run runs the script. Its changes are one undo step. Record records what you do as a script (also Tools > Scripts > Record Macro). Load and Save open and save scripts; Run Script runs a script file. Clear empties the editor; the Output shows what the script prints and its errors. Debugging On the desktop, click in the margin of the editor to set a breakpoint, then click Debug. The script stops at the breakpoint: Continue, Step or Stop it, and type an expression to evaluate it where the script is paused. Script filters A script that defines TraceDrawFilter, with a name, extensions and an Import or Export function, adds a file format to Import and Export. Click Install as Filter to keep it; Script filters lists the installed filters with Edit and Remove. AI assistants (MCP) TraceDraw speaks the Model Context Protocol, so AI assistants on your computer can open, edit, inspect, export and save drawings: tracedraw --mcp runs TraceDraw without a window for an assistant. To let an assistant edit the drawing open in your window, turn on Let AI agents on this computer edit the open drawing (MCP) on the General page of Tools > Options > Global, and give the assistant tracedraw --mcp-window as its command. Each change is one undo step you can take back. Only programs on your computer with the secret token TraceDraw writes can connect. The command-line tool Every download also has tracedraw-cli, which converts drawings between formats without opening the program, for batch work. Macros TraceDraw runs VBA macro projects written for drawing programs (desktop version). Tools > Macros > Load Macro Project adds a project (.gms) or module files (.bas, .cls, .frm); projects are kept and load at start-up. The Macro Manager lists their macros: double-click one or use Tools > Macros > Run Macro (Alt+Shift+F8) to run it. A macro's forms, message boxes and input boxes appear on screen, Esc or Tools > Macros > Stop Macro stops it, and everything one run changes is one undo step. Tools > Macros > Macro Editor (Alt+F11) shows and edits the code. Macros that call Windows functions or the editor's own object model do not run.

h: The Time Tracker toolbar The Time Tracker dialog box
x: Time tracker The time tracker records the time you spend on a drawing, task by task, and keeps the records in the drawing (in .tdraw files). Time counts only while you work: after a few idle minutes the clock waits, and your next action starts it again. The Time Tracker toolbar Window > Toolbars > Time Tracker shows a bar with: the list of tasks, to choose the active task, or add a new one; the time of the active task; the record and pause button; a light: red while counting, amber while idle, gray when paused or without a task; the total of every task; a button that opens the dialog box. Starting the clock on a drawing without tasks adds "Task 1". The Time Tracker dialog box Tools > Time Tracker lists the tasks with their time, start and finish, and the total.  New task, Delete, Make active and Reset time act on the selected task. Double-click a task to make it active. Record and Pause start and stop the clock. Edit the selected task's name, time (such as 1:30:00, 1:30 or 1.5 hours), start and finish (such as 2026-10-19 14:30). Stop counting after N minutes without input sets the idle time (5 minutes at first). Export CSV and Export text save the records, for a spreadsheet or a report. Recording time is not an edit of the drawing: it makes no undo step. The records are saved with the drawing's next save.

The status bar The status bar runs along the bottom of the window (right-click it to move it to the top). From the left: The settings button chooses what the first field shows: tool hints (at first), object details, cursor coordinates or the document's color settings. The first field: a hint for the active tool, the size and center of the selection, the pointer's position, or the color profiles. While you move, scale, rotate or skew objects, it shows the distance, scale or angle. The object information: what is selected and on which layer, such as "Rectangle on Layer 1" or "2 Objects Selected on Layer 1"; with the Shape tool, the number of nodes of a curve. The fill of the selection: a swatch and its description. Double-click it to change the fill. The outline of the selection: a swatch, the color and the width. Double-click it to change the outline. The proof colors button: shows colors as they will print; see Color management. Beside it, a button switches between the light and dark themes. With nothing selected, the fill and outline parts show those of new objects. To show or hide the status bar, use Window > Toolbars > Status Bar.

Glossary Active layer: the layer where new objects go; see Objects and layers. Anchor: a point of an object that connector lines attach to. Artistic text: text placed at a point, one or a few lines. Bleed: the part of a design that runs past the edge of the page, so that nothing white shows once the print is trimmed. Bitmap: a picture made of pixels, such as a photo. Clip frame: a closed object that shows only the part of its contents that lies inside it. CMYK: cyan, magenta, yellow and black, the inks of color printing. Curve: a line or shape made of segments joined at nodes, which you can edit with the Shape tool. Document palette: the colors used in a drawing, collected under the drawing window. Fill: what paints the inside of a closed object. Flyout: a group of related tools behind one toolbox button. Group: several objects that move and resize together. Guideline: a line across the drawing window that objects snap to; it does not print. Live effect: an effect, such as a blend or an envelope, drawn from the object and changeable at any time. Master layer: a layer whose objects show on every page. Node: a point of a curve where two segments meet. Outline: the line along the edge of an object. Panel: a window of settings docked at the side, such as Properties. Paragraph text: text that flows inside a frame. Property bar: the bar that shows the settings of the selection and the active tool. Resolution: how many pixels or dots make an inch (dpi). RGB: red, green and blue, the colors of light on screens. Segment: the part of a curve between two nodes. Spot color: a named ink printed on a plate of its own. Subpath: one connected part of a curve made of several parts. Symbol: an object defined once and placed many times as instances. Vector: drawing made of shapes described by points and curves, which stays sharp at any size.
